learning_objective: The learner will identify seven features of a readable page from a description of how each looks, with at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** readable-page-anatomy
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Remember
**Bloom Verb:** identify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will identify seven features of a readable page from a description of how each looks, with at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Text Structure, Defined Terms, Plain Language (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** In quiz mode the learner clicks the marker that matches a visual hint. A click is correct when it matches the marker named in the Hint column of Content. Mastery is at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt. Hovering in explore mode is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A heading is just larger text. (2) A summary repeats the whole page. (3) Examples make a page longer without helping. **Instructional Rationale:** Identifying features of a page is a Remember-level task, and an illustration of a readable page shows how the features sit together on one page. The quiz asks the learner to recognize each by its look. **Content:** The illustration is a text-free flat drawing of one lesson page. At the top is a wide bar of heading text. Under it is a short block of three thin lines. Further down a single word in the block is highlighted with a small dot beside it. A box with a small lightbulb icon holds two thin lines. A short list of three lines, each with a dot at its left, follows. Next is a framed picture with a thin strip beneath it. At the bottom is a shaded box with two thin lines and a small checkmark icon. The seven markers: | # | Label | Hint (describes the look, not the name) | Description | Tip | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Descriptive heading | The wide bar of text at the top of the page. | A heading that tells the reader what the section is about, in words that match its content. | Write headings as short phrases that say what is inside. | | 2 | Short paragraph | A block of three thin lines under the heading. | A paragraph of three to five sentences with one idea. | Break a paragraph when the idea changes. | | 3 | Defined term | A single highlighted word with a small dot beside it. | A specialized word whose meaning is given where it first appears. | Put the definition in the same sentence. | | 4 | Example box | A box with a small lightbulb icon holding two thin lines. | A concrete example that shows the idea at work. | Use an example whenever an idea is abstract. | | 5 | List | A short list of three lines, each with a dot at its left. | Steps or items set apart, so the reader can scan them. | Use a numbered list when order matters. | | 6 | Figure with caption | A framed picture with a thin strip beneath it. | A picture that supports the text, with a caption that says what to notice. | Describe the figure in the caption and credit its source. | | 7 | Summary box | A shaded box at the bottom with a small checkmark icon. | A short recap of the key points at the end of the section. | Name the two or three ideas a reader should keep. | **Provenance:** The seven features follow the chapter sections "Text Structure", "Defined Terms", and "Plain Language". The illustration is synthetic, and the sim labels the page "illustrative example". **Rules:** Each hint matches exactly one marker. The illustration contains no text, so every label comes from the table above. Markers are numbered 1 to 7 in the order of the table. **Learner Activity:** 1. In explore mode the learner hovers or clicks a marker and reads its label, description, and tip. 2. In quiz mode the sim shows a hint. 3. The learner clicks the marker they think the hint describes. 4. If the first click is wrong, the sim says so and lets the learner try once more. If the second click is also wrong, the sim reveals the marker and its description. 5. After all 7 hints the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 7 hints in a shuffled order, two attempts each. Only a correct first click counts as evidence. Correct: "Correct: [label]. [Description]". First wrong click: "Not quite. Look again at the hint: [hint]". Second wrong click: "This is [label]. [Description]". The summary shows "[n] of 7 correct on the first attempt". At 6 or more it adds "You can read a page's structure." Below 6 it lists the labels of the missed features. **Starting State:** The illustration with seven numbered markers, explore mode active, and the prompt "Hover a marker to see what it is." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's text-structure example lists headings, short paragraphs, lists, signposts, and a summary, and its page features include a defined term, an example box, and a figure with a caption.
